en.title: Count Positive Integers Whose Base-4 Digits Are Only 0 and 1
en.description:
A positive integer is called fancy if its base-4 representation contains only the digits 0 and 1. Given n, count the positive fancy integers strictly less than n; 0 is not counted.

This site's standard input/output protocol was explicitly added by CSWork and does not mean the upstream function-style problem originally had this protocol.
en.input: The input is one integer n (1≤n≤10^9).
en.output: Output the number of positive integers that satisfy the condition.
en.explanation: Process according to the rules; see the accompanying editorial for the approach, proof of correctness and complexity.
hints: Convert n to base 4. First count all valid positive numbers with fewer digits, then go from the most significant digit to the least and count the smaller valid digit combinations available at the current digit; the leading digit can only be 1.
